claims.claim: Provider configs define how PromptArena connects to LLM services and specify authentication, model selection and default parameters
Built-in provider types exist for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google (Gemini) services
Command 'promptarena init my-test --quick --provider openai' creates a project with an OpenAI provider
promptarena init accepts a --quick flag
promptarena init accepts a --provider flag
Running 'promptarena init my-test' without flags prompts interactively for a provider
The interactive init provider prompt offers openai, anthropic, google and mock
init generates a provider config with correct API version and schema, recommended model defaults and a ready-to-use configuration
init sets up environment variables through a .env file
Provider files are placed in a providers/ directory and referenced from arena.yaml
apiVersion value promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1 is the provider manifest version
kind value Provider is a valid manifest kind
metadata.name is a field of a provider manifest
metadata.labels is a map field of a provider manifest, used with provider label values
spec.type is a field of the provider spec
spec.model is a field of the provider spec
spec.capabilities is a list field of the provider spec
spec.defaults accepts temperature, max_tokens and top_p
The openai provider reads the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable automatically
Scenarios accept a required_capabilities field
Capability enum values are text, streaming, vision, tools, json, audio, video, documents and duplex
A scenario with required_capabilities runs only against providers that have ALL listed capabilities
Example vision-capable openai provider uses model gpt-4o with capabilities text, streaming, vision, tools, json
Example audio-only openai provider uses model gpt-4o-audio-preview with capabilities audio and duplex
Example ollama provider with model llama3.2:3b declares capabilities text, streaming, tools, json
llama3.2:3b does not support vision; only the 11B and 90B variants do
Example openai provider 'openai-gpt4o' uses type openai, model gpt-4o, temperature 0.7 and max_tokens 4000
OpenAI available models are gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4-turbo and gpt-3.5-turbo
Example anthropic provider uses type anthropic, model claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, label provider anthropic, temperature 0.6 and max_tokens 4000
The anthropic provider reads the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable automatically
Anthropic available models are claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 and claude-3-opus-20240229
Example gemini provider uses type gemini, model gemini-1.5-flash, label provider google, temperature 0.7 and max_tokens 2000
The gemini provider reads the GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variable automatically
Gemini available models are gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-1.5-flash and gemini-2.0-flash-exp
Azure OpenAI is configured with type openai plus platform authentication of type azure
The provider auto-derives the Azure deployment URL from platform.endpoint and model
spec.platform is a field with type (azure), endpoint and additional_config
platform.additional_config.api_version defaults to 2024-12-01-preview
Azure auth uses the Azure Default Credential chain (Managed Identity, Azure CLI, or environment variables)
AZURE_TENANT_ID is read by the Azure credential chain
AZURE_CLIENT_ID is read by the Azure credential chain
AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET is read by the Azure credential chain
spec.credential with credential_env selects API key auth instead of Azure AD
credential_env accepts AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY as the env var name holding the Azure API key
Azure deployments use the Chat Completions API only; the Responses API is unavailable and the provider falls back to Completions mode
Example ollama provider uses type ollama, model llama3.2:1b, base_url http://localhost:11434, keep_alive 5m, temperature 0.7 and max_tokens 2048
spec.base_url is a field used by the ollama provider
additional_config.keep_alive is an ollama option that keeps the model loaded for a duration such as 5m
The ollama provider needs no API key
Ollama setup commands: 'brew install ollama', 'ollama serve' and 'ollama pull llama3.2:1b'
Docker command runs the ollama/ollama image publishing port 11434
Any model listed by ollama list can be used with the ollama provider (llama3.2:1b, llama3.2:3b, mistral, llava, deepseek-r1:8b)
Example vllm provider uses type vllm, model meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, base_url http://localhost:8000, temperature 0.7 and max_tokens 2048
vllm is a valid provider spec.type
additional_config.use_beam_search is a vLLM option
additional_config.best_of is a vLLM option
additional_config.guided_json is passed through to vLLM for guided JSON decoding
Docker command runs vllm/vllm-openai:latest with --model, --dtype half and --max-model-len flags on port 8000
Docker Compose example runs the vllm/vllm-openai image on port 8000 with NVIDIA GPU reservation
vLLM can serve any HuggingFace model that vLLM supports
additional_config.guided_regex is passed through to vLLM for regex-constrained output
additional_config.guided_choice is passed through to vLLM for choice-constrained output
Inference providers back the runtime/classify task interfaces: audio, text, image and video classifiers and embedders
Inference providers power assertion handlers such as audio_emotion and do not participate in the LLM run matrix
The HuggingFace Inference API is the only shipped inference provider backend
spec.type huggingface is a valid provider type for inference providers
spec.role accepts the value inference, which routes the provider into the classify registry
spec.credential.credential_env HF_TOKEN supplies the HuggingFace token
HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN is accepted as an alternative token env var for HuggingFace
arena.yaml spec.providers entries take id and file fields
spec.defaults.inference accepts audio_classifier, text_classifier, image_classifier and embedder keys
An assertion that omits provider uses defaults.inference.audio_classifier
The classify-backed handler is a pure eval primitive emitting the score for expected_label; wrapping it in type assertion applies the pass/fail threshold
Scenarios accept a conversation_assertions field
type assertion is a valid conversation assertion type
audio_emotion is a valid eval_type
eval_params.model accepts a HuggingFace model id such as superb/wav2vec2-base-superb-er
eval_params.expected_label is a field of audio_emotion
params.min_score is the pass/fail threshold field of the assertion
A HuggingFace 503 model is loading response causes the assertion to be recorded as skipped, not failed
Setting additional_config.dedicated true makes the classify client skip the /models/{owner}/{name} suffix
Example dedicated endpoint sets type huggingface, role inference, base_url, additional_config.dedicated true and credential_env HF_TOKEN
The built-in openai provider can target OpenAI-compatible gateways through base_url and optional headers
headers is a top-level field on the provider spec
Header values are plain strings and headers are injected into every request the provider sends
A custom header that collides with a built-in header (e.g. Authorization, Content-Type) makes the request fail fast with an error
OpenRouter documentation recommends HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers for attribution
Example openrouter provider uses type openai, model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514, base_url https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, headers HTTP-Referer and X-Title, and credential_env OPENROUTER_API_KEY
OPENROUTER_API_KEY is the environment variable holding the OpenRouter key
OpenRouter accepts model identifiers such as openai/gpt-4o-mini, anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514 and meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct
Example groq provider uses type openai, model llama-3.3-70b-versatile, base_url https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 and credential_env GROQ_API_KEY
Groq works with base_url alone and needs no custom headers
Example together provider uses type openai, model meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo, base_url https://api.together.xyz/v1 and credential_env TOGETHER_API_KEY
Example litellm provider uses type openai with base_url http://litellm.internal:4000 and a custom X-Internal-Auth header
Any provider type can declare headers, not only OpenAI-compatible gateways
Custom headers are applied after the provider sets its built-in headers, so collision detection runs before any request is sent
Auth should be set via the credential field rather than by overriding built-in headers
Streaming retry, concurrency limits and connection pool tuning are optional and default to safe values
spec.stream_retry.enabled is a field that turns on streaming retry
stream_retry.max_attempts is a field; the value 2 means initial attempt plus one retry
stream_retry.retry_window accepts pre_first_chunk and always
stream_retry.retry_window defaults to pre_first_chunk
stream_retry.budget.rate_per_sec is a field of the retry budget
stream_retry.budget.burst is a field of the retry budget
retry_window always also retries mid-stream failures by discarding the response and re-requesting from scratch, costing extra tokens
spec.request_timeout is a field for the non-streaming call timeout, accepting a duration string such as 60s
spec.stream_idle_timeout is a field that aborts a stream that goes silent
spec.stream_max_concurrent is a field limiting parallel streams
stream_max_concurrent of 0 means unlimited
spec.http_transport is a field group for connection pool tuning
http_transport.max_conns_per_host defaults to 100
http_transport.max_idle_conns_per_host is a field of the connection pool
http_transport.idle_conn_timeout is a field of the connection pool and accepts a duration such as 90s
The effective concurrent-stream ceiling is max_conns_per_host multiplied by the upstream HTTP/2 max concurrent streams setting
promptkit_http_conns_in_use is a Prometheus gauge tracking connection pool pressure
kind value Arena is a valid arena.yaml manifest kind
arena.yaml spec.prompt_configs entries take id and file fields
Example arena.yaml references providers/openai.yaml, providers/claude.yaml and providers/gemini.yaml under spec.providers
arena.yaml spec.scenarios entries take a file field
OPENAI_API_KEY is the environment variable for OpenAI credentials
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is the environment variable for Anthropic credentials
GOOGLE_API_KEY is the environment variable for Google credentials
promptarena does not load a .env file automatically; the user must export variables before running
Command 'promptarena run' runs the arena tests
Example GitHub Actions workflow passes OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from secrets as env
Example providers openai-gpt4 and openai-mini use labels provider openai with tiers premium and cost-effective
A single providers file may contain multiple provider documents separated by ---
Example openai-creative and openai-precise providers set temperature 0.9 and 0.1 in defaults
promptarena run accepts a --provider flag selecting providers by name
The --provider flag accepts a comma-separated list of provider names
promptarena run without --provider runs all configured providers
Scenario labels such as provider-specific constrain which providers run the scenario
Scenario kind manifest accepts spec.task_type and spec.turns
Scenario turns take role and content fields
promptarena run accepts a --temperature flag
--temperature overrides the temperature for all providers at runtime
promptarena run accepts a --max-tokens flag that overrides max tokens at runtime
Combined overrides --temperature 0.9 --max-tokens 4000 are accepted together
Command 'promptarena config-inspect' lists loaded providers
config-inspect output shows a Providers section listing each provider with its file path
promptarena run accepts a --verbose flag
promptarena config-inspect accepts a --verbose flag
promptarena run accepts a --concurrency flag
--concurrency 1 runs tests sequentially
examples/customer-support/providers/ directory exists
examples/mcp-chatbot/providers/ directory exists
examples/ollama-local/providers/ directory exists and contains a local Ollama setup with Docker
A provider file with a second YAML document after --- fails to load
init writes a .env.example file listing the API key variables to export
